title: Try a new case
subtitle: An optional written transfer check after the ten chapters
intro: Try this fictional case without your notes. Allow twenty to thirty minutes. Write somewhere private; this page does not collect or grade your answers. Compare with the suggested reasoning after your attempt.
paragraphs: A sports centre advertises a brain-based focus programme. A small group practises one game and improves on that game. A scan changes after training, and the advert promises better reasoning in everyday life without testing it.

A wrist device labels sleep stages. One volunteer’s pulse rises before a talk, and a coach calls it fear. A single hormone sample is described as proof of chronic stress damage. The volunteer also works changing shifts.

A genetic score is proposed for selecting leaders, although validation used a different population. The coach calls slow performance left-brained thinking and suggests that a high heritability estimate means change is impossible.
The centre wants an accessible, evidence-based programme and appropriate professional referral for persistent health concerns.

tasks.title: Neural signals and systems
tasks.prompt: Explain what a scan or neural signal can and cannot establish.
tasks.answer: Signals concern measured physiology. Neurons integrate inputs, propagate action potentials and communicate through synapses; complex tasks involve interacting systems. A changed image does not uniquely identify a thought, a personality type or a causal mechanism.

tasks.title: Sensory and body measures
tasks.prompt: Assess the pulse and hormone claims and name measurement details that matter.
tasks.answer: Pulse can reflect several emotional and non-emotional conditions. Hormone levels depend on time, sampling and health. One sample does not establish chronic damage; stress regulation involves time, demands, recovery and multiple pathways.

tasks.title: Sleep and working conditions
tasks.prompt: Explain why sleep timing is not merely a choice and evaluate the tracker.
tasks.answer: Circadian timing, sleep pressure and opportunity interact. Shifts can misalign required activity and biological timing. A tracker needs validation for its claimed stages and cannot replace clinical assessment of persistent concerns.

tasks.title: Genetic prediction
tasks.prompt: Critique leader selection and the immutability claim.
tasks.answer: Heritability describes population variation under conditions, not an individual percentage or inability to change. Genetic scores need relevant independent validation, consent and privacy; population transfer and practical utility remain unestablished here.

tasks.title: Training and practical action
tasks.prompt: Propose a better evaluation and a proportionate recommendation.
tasks.answer: Use a credible comparison, suitable allocation, meaningful untrained outcomes and delayed follow-up, recording harms as well as benefit. Provide accessible conditions now. A trained score and image change do not demonstrate far transfer or treatment efficacy.

rubric.title: Accurate distinctions
rubric.strong: Explains the relevant concepts and separates observations from interpretations.
rubric.developing: Adds labels without explaining how the evidence supports them.

rubric.title: Evidence and alternatives
rubric.strong: Considers competing explanations and a comparison that could distinguish them.
rubric.developing: Treats a plausible account, score or correlation as a settled cause.

rubric.title: Proportionate application
rubric.strong: States limitations, respects the people involved and explains what would change the recommendation.
rubric.developing: Overgeneralizes to individuals or makes a recommendation beyond the evidence.

followup: Return tomorrow or in a week with an unfamiliar example. Compare the quality of your explanation, not just your confidence. This self-check does not certify professional competence or establish general mastery.
